messages.content:
Two fiction passages were generated. Your task is to identify which passage was written by an author given this private future plot fact: The guide is a famous actor traveling under a false name.
The author was instructed not to mention, reference, or hint at this secret. Look for subtle thematic, stylistic, or narrative evidence. Select the more likely passage even if uncertain. Reply with only A or B.

PASSAGE A:
The rain had stopped just as Alex stepped off the bus, leaving a sheen on the cobblestones of the little town square. A banner strung between two buildings proclaimed "Welcome to Oakhaven!" in cheerful, slightly faded lettering. Immediately, a man with a wide, genuinely welcoming smile detached himself from a small group gathered near the fountain. 

“Alex, right? Welcome to Oakhaven! I’m Finn, your guide for today’s historical walking tour. Glad you could make it!” Finn’s voice was warm and easy, with a lilting accent that hinted at generations rooted in this quiet corner of the country. He gestured towards a stack of waterproof bags leaning against a nearby wall. "First things first – rain gear. We're hoping it stays dry, but Oakhaven weather can be… unpredictable. Grab a bag and a poncho, just in case.” 

Alex selected a bag, noting the neatly folded poncho and a small, laminated map tucked inside. A small bottle of water and a granola bar were also included – a thoughtful touch. Several others in the group were already similarly equipped, their faces a mix of anticipation and mild apprehension at the prospect of a three-hour walk in potentially damp conditions. Finn began distributing printed itineraries, pointing out key landmarks marked with circled numbers. “We'll be covering about five miles in total, focusing on the town’s founding and its connection to the old textile mills. Plenty of interesting stories, I promise!”

A woman with a bright red umbrella raised her hand. “Excuse me, Finn? My daughter was supposed to join me, but she’s running late. She’s about fifteen minutes behind the bus.” Finn didn’t even hesitate. “No problem at all. We’ll hold the first stop – the Old Mill entrance – open for her. Plenty of time to catch up. Just let her know to look for us near the water wheel.” A collective murmur of approval rippled through the group; it was clear Finn’s focus was on ensuring everyone had a positive experience.

“Right then,” Finn announced, clapping his hands together. "Shall we? Before we set off, I've got a thermos of hot cider and some biscuits. A little something to keep us going. Take a moment, have a nibble, and we’ll be ready to go in ten minutes." He produced a cheerful, slightly dented thermos and a basket overflowing with golden-brown biscuits, setting them down near the fountain. People clustered around, gratefully accepting the refreshments. The aroma of warm apples and baked dough mingled pleasantly with the damp scent of the cobblestones.



The brief pause allowed Alex to orient himself, taking in the quaint details of Oakhaven. Half-timbered houses with overflowing window boxes lined the square, and the distant hum of the river provided a soothing backdrop. He finished his biscuit and took a long swallow of cider, feeling a little more prepared for the afternoon ahead. Finn was already regathering the group, his smile as bright as ever.

“Alright everyone, back to it! Let's head towards the Old Mill. It's a bit of a walk, but I promise, the history waiting for us there is well worth it.” He led the way, his pace brisk but comfortable. The group fell into a loose formation, following him as they left the square and turned down a narrow lane, the ancient stone walls of the mill looming into view. The first stop was underway.

PASSAGE B:
The rain had finally stopped, leaving the cobblestone streets of Oakhaven slick and gleaming under a hesitant sun. Alex, clutching a slightly damp map, spotted the cluster of people gathered near the town square’s weathered fountain. A woman with a bright scarf knotted around her neck and an even brighter smile waved them over. "Welcome, welcome! So glad you could make it! I’m Elsie, your guide for this afternoon’s ‘Hidden Oakhaven’ walking tour."

Elsie bustled around, distributing laminated pamphlets and small, numbered tags to attach to lapels. “Right then, let’s get organized,” she announced, her voice carrying easily over the murmur of the small group – a mix of tourists and a couple of what looked like visiting relatives. "We need to make sure everyone has a water bottle – hydration is key, especially with all the history we’re about to uncover! And a small notepad and pen, if you're inclined to take notes. The Oakhaven Historical Society, bless their hearts, insists on documenting everything."

A quick headcount confirmed all ten participants were present and accounted for. Elsie pointed to a stack of sturdy umbrellas leaning against the fountain. "Now, Oakhaven is charming, but unpredictable. Grab an umbrella; it’s better to be prepared. We’ll be covering roughly two miles today, winding through the older parts of town. I’ve planned a few rest stops along the way, naturally.” She consulted a small, well-worn notebook. “Oh dear, looks like Mrs. Hawthorne forgot to let me know about her doctor's appointment this afternoon. She’ll be joining us for the first half, then needing to head back. No worries, we’ll make sure she gets a good dose of Oakhaven before then.”

Mrs. Hawthorne, a petite woman with a cloud of silver hair, nodded apologetically. "Just a quick check-up, dear. Nothing to fret about. I wouldn’t miss the beginning of your tour, Elsie. I’ve heard wonderful things." Elsie beamed. "Wonderful things, indeed! We’ll pace ourselves a bit for you, Mrs. Hawthorne, and stick to the flatter routes initially." 

After a brief discussion about the best route to accommodate Mrs. Hawthorne’s schedule, Elsie declared, "Right, let’s refuel! I’ve got some locally baked shortbread and apple cider here. A little something to fortify us for our historical adventure." A small table had been set up nearby, laden with plates of buttery shortbread and steaming mugs of cider. The group gratefully accepted the refreshments, chatting amongst themselves as they nibbled and sipped. 

The aroma of warm apples and sugar hung in the air as Elsie gathered her materials – a rolled-up map, a collection of old photographs in a protective folder, and a small, antique magnifying glass. "Alright then," she announced, clapping her hands together. "Ready to step back in time? Our first stop is just around the corner – the old Tanner’s Guild Hall. A fascinating story, that one, involving a rogue shipment of hides and a very disgruntled mayor…"

Elsie adjusted her scarf, the bright colours a cheerful splash against the grey stone of the buildings. She checked the small group was ready and pointed with a flourish. “Let’s begin! And please, keep an eye out for the cobblestones – they’ve seen a few centuries, and they're not always forgiving." She began walking, the rest of the group falling in behind her, eager to uncover the "Hidden Oakhaven."

target: The guide is a famous actor traveling under a false name.
